description.p: Flux is a minimalist, high-performance file manager built with Rust, GTK4, and Libadwaita. Engineered for keyboard-centric power users, it pairs a clean GNOME aesthetic with an asynchronous architecture that prevents UI freezes.

ul.li: Fast sub-150ms startup time backed by a non-blocking asynchronous pipeline
Instant live search with deep body queries and mathematical size filters (>10MB, <500KB, ranges)
Global tag navigation with SQLite indexing via FreeDesktop extended attributes
Integrated terminal pane with automatic OSC 7 working directory synchronization
Direct virtual archive navigation for zip, 7z, rar, tarballs, and ISO images without pre-extraction
Encrypted storage and remote mounts supporting LUKS containers and GVFS protocols (SMB, SFTP, NFS, WebDAV, Google Drive)
Triage panel to temporarily pin, cycle, and organize directories across workspaces
File operations safety net featuring undo/redo queues, conflict policies, and root deletion guards
Deep file inspector displaying Shannon entropy, SHA-256 hashes, media specs, and Git history
Configurable dual view modes (responsive card grid and list) with dynamic headers and custom icon badges
